audit.why: EVEN / 6-10 with a 7/10 carry rating matches a 50% win rate and the page's own honest framing: two tanks, neither with the damage to close a duel. The lane is decided off the 1v1.
audit.corrected: No change to diff, tone, diffRating or carryRating.
sources: content late: 'Two tanks with no kill pressure — this is a stalemate by design'

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3 and 4 said Skill while their whys give both stages to Maokai, and row 6 said Maokai while its why calls the stage a stalemate.
audit.why: whys[3] 'the wave control and short-trade edge stays on his side through 4-5'; whys[4] 'he survives the lockdown'; whys[6] 'Two tanks with no kill damage stalemate the lane'. The packet chart reads Skill/Maokai/Maokai/Maokai/Maokai/Maokai/Skill and the mirror audit set rows 3 and 4 to Maokai and row 6 to Skill on its side.
audit.corrected: Rows 3 and 4 flipped to Maokai and row 6 to Skill as matched full+content pairs, with the three why strings rewritten to carry real cooldowns. Existing ratings already fit the new owners.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Twisted Advance purely as a root-dash and never mentions that Maokai is untargetable for its whole travel, so a Depth Charge or hook spent into it is simply lost. Nature's Grasp is also described as a knockback when it is an advancing wall that roots, and its 3000 range is never stated.
audit.why: enemyKit W: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target' — 14/13/12/11/10s. That untargetability is the single reason a 120s Depth Charge can be wasted here, and the missingInteractions file flags untargetable-dodges-burst for exactly this. enemyKit R: 'summons a colossal wall of brambles and thorns that slowly advances forwards, damaging and rooting', range 3000 — with no dash on Nautilus, the flagged terrain-cuts-retreat rule means Flash is held for the wall, not for damage.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance's untargetability and 14s rank-1 cooldown written into dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and phases[4].why; Nature's Grasp restated as a 3000-range advancing root wall in dontsFull[2].d.
sources: enemyKit W/R text, ranges, cooldowns and flags

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Twisted Advance's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His sapling sustain heals through your W burn — Sapling Toss is 18s at rank 1, so the short-trade edge stays with him through 4-5.

edits.before: Depth Charge is an unmissable point-click knockup — the all-in always starts. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Maokai's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Depth Charge cannot miss, but Twisted Advance makes him untargetable mid-dash and Nature's Grasp roots you — a 1v1 at 6 trades even at best.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Maokai carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two tanks with no kill damage stalemate the lane — it resolves on your R picks and roams, not on the side-lane duel.

edits.before: His lock-on root. Dodge/peel it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1 and untargetable in flight — wait it out.

edits.before: Whiffing hook and walking forward anyway — your kill threat IS the hook; without it you are a slow shield.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp is a 3000-range advancing wall that roots — you have no dash, so hold Flash for it.

edits.before: Track Maokai's Twisted Advance (Root): His lock-on root. Dodge/peel it. When it is down — Q-E + R him.
edits.after: Twisted Advance goes untargetable mid-dash — never spend Depth Charge into it. It is 14s at rank 1.

notes: dontsFull[2].t reads 'Eat his R knockback' and report[11].t repeats it. Nature's Grasp roots; the knockback in Maokai's kit is Bramble Smash (Q). Both strings are under 25 characters or embedded in a list I could not fix without breaking the length band, so the wrong label survives in the Common Mistakes line — worth a follow-up. Anti-heal advice on this page is correct and supported: Sap Magic (P) heals him on his empowered attack and the cooldown shortens every time he casts or is hit by a spell, so a Nautilus who chains W splash and E waves is actively accelerating his sustain.
